column1: # matrix.tsv -- the declaration BOTH runners walk. One row is one run.
# Neither RUN_ME_FIRST.praat nor run_analyses.R carries its own list of
# analyses. Both read this file. That is the point: a cell that exists on one
# side and not the other cannot happen, and adding a cell is one line here
# rather than two edits in two languages.
# DERIVED, NOT INVENTED. Every axis below came out of the source:
#   test / adjustment / post-hoc / equal-variance / group-order values are the
#     if/elsif ladders those wrappers use to build the orchestrator arguments.
#     (survey lane, which has no dialog and no menu item).
#   datasets are the committed evidence/csv/*.csv, mapped to analyses by their
#     own columns and by which validate/v*.R reads them.
#   cell_id      stable identifier; never reused, never renumbered in place
#   procedure    the Praat procedure to call, exactly as it is defined
#   dataset      file stem in data/ (analysis lane) or the fixture (survey)
#   col_a        1st column argument: dataCol / col1 / colX / depCol /
#                predCol, or the pipe-delimited condition list for the
#                repeated-measures pair, or the case label for Wilson
#   col_b        2nd column argument: groupCol / col2 / colY / factor1 / respCol
#   col_c        3rd: factor2, or the grouping column for grouped regression
#   test         the test-selecting argument, verbatim as passed; empty where
#                the procedure has no test axis
#   posthoc      post-hoc selector as passed: 0/1 for doTukey, doDunn and
#                doPostHoc; empty where the procedure has none
#   adjust       bonferroni | holm | bh | none; empty where not taken
#                empty where the procedure never calls @emlCountGroups
#   prereq       a call that must run first in the same session, "proc:args"
#   expect       ok | refuse -- a refusal that happens correctly is evidence
#   note         why this cell is here, or why it refuses
#   study         options | sweep | nist -- which body of evidence this cell
#                  options  the 624 cells above -- the plugin's own option space,
#                  sweep    the designed shape grid, k in {2,3,5} x balance x
#                           oracled against base R in run_analyses.R like any
#                  nist     NIST StRD certified ANOVA datasets
#                           compares the Praat column against nist_certified.tsv's
#                compare.R's balance invariant runs per study and in total, so a
#                row cannot escape by being filed under the wrong one.
# GROUP ORDER IS RESULT-AFFECTING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN AXIS.
# Measured on Praat 6.6.30, v11_twoway_input, SPL_dB by voice_type:
# Same data, same test, opposite sign. The same flip reaches Cohen's d,
# rank-biserial r and every Tukey mean difference.
# WHAT IS BOUNDED, AND WHY. A silent cap reads as complete coverage.
#   B1 22 committed *_input.csv names hold 17 distinct contents. Byte-identical
#      files are run once. Collapsed aliases, by md5:
#   B2 Two-group (testType x equalVar) is a 3x2 grid; only 4 cells are
#      reachable from any door, and equalVar is read only inside the
#      parametric arm, so (nonparametric,1) and (both,1) are exact duplicates
#   B3 Scheffe is bound to adjust=none. @emlScheffe takes no adjustment; the
#      value would only change a line of report text. 3 cells -> 1, which is
#      the value the wizard itself passes for that row.
#   B4 With the post hoc off, .adjMethod$ is unread -- it sits inside
#   B5 Normality's .testType$ selects no test; its own header says so, and
#      says "both" and "auto" behave identically. Bound to "both".
#   B6 On the k-group family only the two real measurement columns (SPL_dB,
#      vibrato_rate_Hz) are used as responses. Identifier columns are not
#   B7 Refusal cells are not crossed against group order: a refusal on group
#      COUNT cannot depend on the order the groups were counted in.
#   B8 group_order is left empty where the procedure never calls
#      regression, normality, RM-ANOVA, Friedman, and two-way ANOVA (which
#   B9 Grouped CORRELATION is absent. It has no analysis-layer procedure: it
#      is assembled inline in scripts/eml-correlate.praat. Grouped REGRESSION
#   B10 Wilson is crossed at the three levels the committed fixture itself
#      names (0.90, 0.95, 0.99) rather than at each row's single stored conf.
# TWO CELLS THAT USED TO ABORT INSTEAD OF REFUSING -- FIXED AT THE SOURCE.
# c0418 and c0419 are marked expect=refuse. On Praat 6.6.30 they used to take
#            four guards. Its record hook at label END_CORR reads it on every
#            refusal path. Every sibling orchestrator initialises it on entry.
#   D-CORR-2 @emlPearsonCorrelation set its numeric outputs only when
#            .error$ is empty. Its own sibling @emlPearsonCorrelationAlt, five
#            lines below in the same file, initialises them to undefined
#            first, and so does @emlSpearmanCorrelation. On zero-variance
#            input the caller's next line read an unassigned .r.
# Both are now fixed in the plugin itself (plugin_EML_StatsGraphs/stats/
# eml-analysis.praat and stats/eml-inferential.praat): each initialises its
# outputs to undefined at entry, matching its siblings. c0418 and c0419 now
# THE SURVEY LANE RUNS ON THE INSTALLED PLUGIN, LIKE EVERYTHING ELSE. The kit
# no longer carries its own copy of the library -- RUN_ME_FIRST.praat includes
# the plugin's generated barrel, which carries all fourteen modules, including
# nothing left to rebuild for the survey rows to run.
